Quote sources

Mencius quote sources

12 passages attributed to Mencius in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Mencius.

Quote source / Mencius

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

Sourcing profile

Language of the works
Classical Chinese
Cited here from
The Mengzi, cited by book — Gaozi I and II, Jinxin I and II, Lilou, Gongsun Chou, Teng Wen Gong, Liang Hui Wang.
How to cite it
Book and passage, with the translator named. The Chinese book titles are conventionally kept in romanisation in English citation, so “Mencius, Gaozi II” identifies the roll even in a translation that calls it something else.
Where quotations of this author go wrong
The Mengzi is a compiled record of Mencius' conversations and arguments, not a book he sat down and wrote, and the English title “Mencius” names both the man and the text. A sentence beginning “Mencius said” is a citation convention, not an eyewitness claim.

2 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I check quotations attributed to Mencius?

Book and passage, with the translator named. The Chinese book titles are conventionally kept in romanisation in English citation, so “Mencius, Gaozi II” identifies the roll even in a translation that calls it something else. This archive cites Mencius from The Mengzi, cited by book — Gaozi I and II, Jinxin I and II, Lilou, Gongsun Chou, Teng Wen Gong, Liang Hui Wang. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

What is the most common mistake when quoting Mencius?

The Mengzi is a compiled record of Mencius' conversations and arguments, not a book he sat down and wrote, and the English title “Mencius” names both the man and the text. A sentence beginning “Mencius said” is a citation convention, not an eyewitness claim.

What language did Mencius write in?

Classical Chinese. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
